title: Fixed threshold-four support crossing from d=17 to d=18
question: Does the unchanged d=17 threshold-four core remain valid at d=18 under the same V=2, beta, orientation, row kind and emission rule?
method: Load the hash-pinned R-435 and R-436 manifests and their primary and independent run JSON authorities.
Compare the same V=2, beta=8, right-oriented unconditional one-site marginal row with emission ordinal zero and threshold four.
Read directed interval endpoints for index four and verify d=17 upper < 4 < d=18 lower without rounding.
Check the d=17 and d=18 core/tail splits independently, then run hostile mutations and Lean scalar threshold checks.
Keep the result finite, claim-nonbearing and separate from any increasing-core or full-sector route.
decision_reason: Advance a route-local finite boundary: unchanged fixed-support reuse is rejected because one declared index crosses the threshold. The observation does not reject increasing-core, cutoff-dependent or full-sector constructions.
decision_scope: V=2, beta=8, right orientation, unconditional one-site marginal, emission ordinal zero, d=17 versus d=18, threshold-four support classification.
boundary: R-437 is T0 finite evidence only. It closes no uniform tail modulus, common core, OS/KMS/GNS gap, continuum, physical-empty sign, Yang-Mills claim or mass-gap statement.
next_action: Specify an increasing-core rule before further cutoff evaluations and seek an owner-approved cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform tail modulus or full-sector completeness theorem.

adversarial_review.check: Both manifests and runs agree on V=2, beta=8, right orientation, unconditional row, ordinal zero and threshold four.
Directed endpoints satisfy d17 upper < 4 < d18 lower; no rounded point estimate is used.
Primary and independent lanes both place index four in d17 core and d18 tail.
The manifest keeps increasing-core and full-sector routes open and rejects only unchanged fixed support.
No common core, physical reference, limit order theorem or Yang-Mills map is supplied.

no_overclaim: R-437 advances only one finite fixed-support boundary audit. It does not establish cutoff/volume uniformity, a tail modulus, physical-empty stationarity or stability, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills dynamics or a mass gap.
